subject: Vendor comparison heatmap + short runbook (post-demo recap)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Vendor comparison heatmap + short runbook (post-demo recap)

Emma / John — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed runbook so we’re all aligned on next steps.

1) Key pain points you reiterated
- Latency variability during peak batch scoring (affects SLAs to trading customers)
- Cost unpredictability when models scale to >100M tokens/month
- Data residency & auditability requirements for EU customers
- Need for simple rollout testing (canary + immediate fallback)

2) Decision criteria you said matter most (priority order)
- Latency p95 under real traffic (target: <= 250ms for short prompts)
- End-to-end cost per 1M tokens including caching/batch effects
- Security/compliance posture (SOCs, audit logs, on-prem/VPC options)
- Operational ergonomics (SDKs, tracing, per-route dashboards)

3) Competitive context you called out
- Vendor A (LargeLab): strong latency in single-region, weaker private deployment options
- Vendor B (CloudAI): integrated data-residency pitch + lower published price, unclear on multi-tenant tail latency

4) Proposed follow-up tests (short runbook) — what I’ll execute with your team next:
- A: Head-to-head latency benchmark: 10k sampled requests (mix of short/long) at 50/100 concurrent sessions; record p50/p95/p99
- B: Cost projection: run your sample monthly workload through our cost model + two competitor estimates — produce flat monthly delta
- C: Security checklist: we’ll scope SOC2 artifacts and provide a private deployment options brief

Attachments: runbook-vendor-heatmap.xlsx (benchmark matrix), redwood-demo-recording.mp4

Requested from you: please confirm procurement and security contacts to loop in (I’ve tentatively added John). Also confirm whether the team can provide a 1–2 week sample query logfile for realistic load shaping.

Proposed timeline: week of Aug 3 — run a remote, live micro-benchmark and walk through results Aug 6–7. If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — we’ll keep the scope narrow so this is replicable on all vendors.

—
Aditya Rao

Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 08:30:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: Vendor comparison heatmap + short runbook (post-demo recap) — internal notes

Aditya / Connor — quick internal note after reviewing the Finex thread and attachments. Summary heatmap (top-line):

- Redwood (us):
  * Pros: predictable tail-latency controls (batching + cache), Private/VPC option, per-route tracing + token-level cost breakdowns
  * Cons: slightly more ops work for on-prem installs than Vendor B’s managed EU product; pricing needs to be shown net of caching gains

- Vendor A (LargeLab):
  * Pros: very competitive single-region latency; mature single-node optimizations
  * Cons: weak audit logs and limited private deployment docs

- Vendor B (CloudAI):
  * Pros: marketed as single-tenant EU offering; aggressive list pricing
  * Cons: unclear on p95 under high multiplexed traffic and how fallback works across regions

Open technical questions to close before benchmark run:
- Does Vendor B actually allow long-term KV-cache snapshots for warm starts? (Impact on cold-start p95)
- What are the exact concurrency and sequence-length distributions Finex will provide? We need those to parameterize kernels and batching policies.
- Can we get an anonymized sample with time-of-day traffic spikes so our run simulates tail load?

Proposed internal test plan (minimal):
1) Use bench-instructions.md to run three replicas: Redwood baseline, Vendor A, Vendor B. Test harness: 10k queries, 50/100 conc, two prompt-length buckets (short <64 tokens, long 256–512).
2) Collect p50/p95/p99, per-token cost estimate, and memory/GPU util per run.
3) Deliver a 1-page heatmap + a 2-page appendix with raw logs for Finex to review.

I’ll carve out capacity on Aug 3–6 to run these (need Connor to assist with the Vendor B config). Attaching bench-instructions.md.

—
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
